key_tile_base_coeffs.unit: cells per S*C, per C, per S
key_tile_base_coeffs.note: The prefix key tile's committed cells at the 8B model's attention width, as the (S*C, C, S) triple the cost model reads: cells = 64 S C + 12288 C + 128 S. Solved from the three points above, whose key tiles cost 64 (S C + S^2) + 12288 C + 12416 S in total; the triple is that total under the composition the cost model itself uses, a prefix key tile at (S, C) plus the same tile at (S, S) with the per-token component dropped. Every coefficient is an identity of the layout at 32 heads of 128: 64 is two per head, 12288 is three per head and channel, 128 is four per head. With the context equal to the block length the C and S columns are the same quantity, so the point at a block of 256 with a prefix of 4,096 is what separates them; three points and three coefficients is an exact solve, so the residual is zero by construction and is not a check of the form. The proofs are made on the host's cores under the reference backend and the card is idle throughout; the machine reports an H200, which is what the run id names, and no timing figure from this run is recorded. A cell count does not depend on the card.

block_c4096.note: The fresh cells of the 32 layer segments of one token block over the 512 positions that block proves: 44,557,347,792 cells over 512, block B8, the one block of the sequence whose prefix is the whole context. It is what the cost model's registration compares its layers-only prediction per decoded token against, and the block is the comparison the prediction means: the model prices 32 layers at the full context, where the earlier blocks of the sequence read a shorter prefix and cost less. The output head segment is not in it; layer segment B8L0 is, with the embedding lookup and the one extra cell an attention-output accumulator it carries, 41,168 cells a position between them. The same 32 segments proved again for the reduction ablation come to the same integer, `cells.ablation.c4096.all_five`. It is a larger figure than `cells_per_position.headline.c4096.base` and its two companions added up, which divide every segment of the run, output heads and short prefixes included, by every position the run proves.

block_c16384.note: The fresh cells of the 32 layer segments of one token block over the 512 positions that block proves: 71,753,215,328 cells over 512, block B32, the one block of the sequence whose prefix is the whole context, on the same terms as the row at context 4,096: the output head segment is out, layer segment B32L0 is in with the embedding lookup and the one extra cell an attention-output accumulator it carries, and the earlier blocks of the sequence read a shorter prefix and are not in it. It is what the cost model's registration compares its layers-only prediction per decoded token against at this context.

logup_marginal_cells_per_lookup.note: recorded as an object keyed by the LogUp batch size as a string, {"1": 4.0, "2": 2.0} -- the marginal is one number per batch size and the model indexes it by the batch it charges

weight_freivalds_cells_per_weight.note: The weight Freivalds check's committed cells per weight, at the prover's own default row width: `result.points[0].cells.cells_per_weight` of runs/2026-09-11-microbench-cells-h100/b3-freivalds.json. Its three QM31 accumulator columns cost 12 cells a trace row and a row carries p weights, so the law is 12/p and p is a layout knob, not a constant of the gadget: this is 12/136, the default of `params_of`. The sweep beside it, b3-freivalds-widths.json, returns 12/p to the cell at 8, 16, 32 and 64 weights a row, which is what says the closed form holds rather than assuming it. A group of n matmuls shares one accumulator and so costs (4 + 8n)/(n p) per weight and not 12/p, which the cost model does not know: charging 12/p across a layer over-charges the two-matmul group by 20 per cent and the three-matmul one by 29. The private archive's 0.0902 is 12/133, the same law at a shape whose grid padded 32,256 rows up to 2^15, so it is this figure inflated 2.3 per cent by row padding and not a second measurement; this subcommand refuses a ragged tiling and reports the unpadded form.

preprocessed_cells_per_weight.note: The preprocessed side of the same check at the same row width, the trace a proof reads once rather than commits again: `result.points[0].cells.preprocessed_per_weight` of runs/2026-09-11-microbench-cells-h100/b3-freivalds.json. It is exactly 1 + 4/p -- one cell a weight, plus the four selectors amortised over a row -- at 8, 16, 32, 64 and 136 weights a row, so it is the same closed form as the fresh figure beside it. Each point is a marginal over the weights two output widths differ by and carries no row padding; the private archive's 1.0903 is one padded component divided by its weights, from a component that also carried nine preprocessed columns beside its weights where this one carries four. The preprocessed trace is in none of the cost model's cell totals, so this figure moves `moe.<model>.preprocessed_over_fresh` and nothing else.

int8_range_cells_per_activation.note: model_constants.logup_marginal_cells_per_lookup['2'] / 2. The range check on a committed int8 activation is one arity-2 lookup into the 2^16 byte-pair table covering two activations, at the batch size every use side finalizes with; the activations' own committed cells are charged elsewhere. The private archive measured the same 1.0 directly at three sizes, and the byte-at-a-time form it replaced is 2.0.

requant_cells_per_value.note: One requantized value with its scale argument, the marginal cells with the shared tables left out and the two committed input cells left out because the producer commits them. The subcommand proves four points: 8.0625 and 11.4375 for power-of-two scales without and with the argument, 8.125 and 11.5 for bf16. The cost model takes the largest of the two with the argument and charges one less than it per distinct matmul input, because the committed quantized value is already counted.

argmax_marginal_cells_per_comparison.note: the whole-gadget key is not this quantity

route_selection_cells.note: nobody has built this gadget; the nearest gadget that was measured stands in for it

route_topk_cells.note: nobody has built this gadget; the nearest gadget that was measured stands in for it

dequant_chain_cells_per_acc.note: Dequantization by the bf16 chain, on the same sweep and the same terms as the power-of-two row above. It costs 1.73 times as much per accumulator.

dequant_chain_away_cells_per_acc.note: Dequantization by the bf16 chain at the rounding away from zero, the marginal cells one accumulator adds with the shared tables left out; 1,048,576 accumulators, 16 per row, from the `chain` point's `cells_per_acc_marginal` in runs/2026-09-11-microbench-cells-h100/b6-dequant-away.json. This is what the cost model charges on all seven layer matmuls, because rounding away from zero is what the quantization configuration specifies and what every recorded proof builds. `model_constants.dequant_chain_cells_per_acc` is the same gadget at the round half to even, 26.125, exactly one cell an accumulator more, and is not this.

dequant_pow2_cells_per_acc.note: Dequantization by a power-of-two scale, the marginal cells one accumulator adds with the shared tables left out; 1,048,576 accumulators, 16 per row. The tables are a fixed cost of the segment and are not multiplied by a count, which is why the marginal figure and not the with-tables one is the cost model's input.

dequant_pow2_away_cells_per_acc.note: Dequantization by a power-of-two scale at the rounding away from zero, on the same sweep and the same terms as the chain entry above, from the `pow2` point's `cells_per_acc_marginal` in runs/2026-09-11-microbench-cells-h100/b6-dequant-away.json. The cost model charges it on the output head. `model_constants.dequant_pow2_cells_per_acc` is the round half to even, 15.0625, again exactly one cell an accumulator more.

attnout_int8_cells_per_acc.note: The attention output's own dequantization, folded straight to int8 because its consumer requantizes it anyway: one rounding per output element, on the same sweep and the same terms as the two rows above. The cost model multiplies it by the attention outputs of every layer and head.

dequant_chain_away_base_cells_per_acc.note: the chain rung's committed columns, no LogUp running sums: what `--gkr-dequant` builds

dequant_pow2_away_base_cells_per_acc.note: the power-of-two rung's committed columns, no LogUp running sums

residual_stream_mul_cells_per_op.note: One bf16 multiply of the residual stream, on the same terms as the add above. The cost model multiplies it by the two multiplies of every normalisation and by the SwiGLU's product. The SiLU in front of the product does not move it, and the normalisation's own scale is 8.4375 because its second operand is a preprocessed weight.

unary_cells_per_application.note: 2 + model_constants.logup_marginal_cells_per_lookup['2']. One bf16 unary operation commits its output as one bf16 value, which is two cells, and pays one lookup at pairwise batching. The cost model multiplies it by each normalisation's square and inverse square root and by the SwiGLU's SiLU. The prover reports the same figure under primitives.unary of the residual-stream output, built from the same two terms, so it is an exact count and not a second measurement.

residual_stream_add_cells_per_op.note: One correctly rounded bf16 add of the residual stream, the marginal cells with the shared tables and the component's leaves left out. The cost model multiplies it by the two residual adds of every layer and by the adds of each normalisation's reduction. Putting a unary operation in front of the add does not move it: the same 24.3226 with a square on every leaf.

attention_cells_per_head_key_token.note: What one entry of the attention score grid costs: the committed shift, the exponential's answer and the probability, over 512 tokens and 1,024 keys at head dimension 64. It is exactly 4 at all five instance counts the run packs, 1 through 16, so it is the grid's own price and not an artefact of one packing. It is the whole of the attention term only in the superseded single-slope form; the key tile coefficients are what the cost model charges, and they carry a per-key and a per-token cost this number does not.

composed_attnout.note: 21,757,952 cells over 2,097,152 attention-output accumulators on all 62 recorded 8B layer chunks at both contexts, at the registered statement; a re-fit against one shape. the attention-output fold. Layer 0 builds one cell an accumulator more than every other layer and is not in the 62.

composed_dequant.note: 353,632,256 cells over 22,020,096 matmul accumulators on all 62 recorded 8B layer chunks at both contexts, at the registered statement; a re-fit against one shape. the whole dequant family: the committed accumulator, the chain rounding and what the reduction leaves in the interaction trace. The standalone chain rung is 25.125 or 26.125 depending on the rounding and commits its own LogUp running sums.

composed_freivalds.note: 44,040,192 cells over 218,103,808 weights on all 62 recorded 8B layer chunks at both contexts, at the registered statement; a re-fit against one shape. B3's width sweep put the standalone check at 0.0902 cells a weight at its own design point; the composed check at this statement is more than twice that, and most of the difference is interaction the reduction does not remove.

composed_quant.note: 45,875,200 cells over 2,621,440 attention q or k values on all 62 recorded 8B layer chunks at both contexts, at the registered statement; a re-fit against one shape. the q and k quantize, which no reduction owns and no key names at all.

composed_requant.note: 212,664,832 cells over 11,534,336 distinct matmul input values on all 62 recorded 8B layer chunks at both contexts, at the registered statement; a re-fit against one shape. the whole requantize family, the multiplicity column of its own tables included. `model_constants.requant_cells_per_value` is the standalone gadget and is not this.

composed_residual_stream_add.note: 47,185,920 cells over 2,621,440 bf16 adds on all 62 recorded 8B layer chunks at both contexts, at the registered statement; a re-fit against one shape. read off RoPE's own add per rotated value (`rpqa`, `rpka`).

composed_residual_stream_mul.note: 26,214,400 cells over 5,242,880 bf16 multiplys on all 62 recorded 8B layer chunks at both contexts, at the registered statement; a re-fit against one shape. read off RoPE's own two multiplies per rotated value (`rpqm`, `rpkm`), which are the only bf16 multiplies in the chunk whose op count the run reports on their own.

composed_residual_stream_unary_plus_mul.note: 73,400,320 cells over 7,340,032 SwiGLU channels on all 62 recorded 8B layer chunks at both contexts, at the registered statement; a re-fit against one shape. one `silu` table application and one bf16 product per channel (`gsw`); the unary on its own is this less the multiply above.

gkrlink_cells_per_chunk.note: the batched reductions' link. 16 cells per row over the reduced components' heights on both recorded 8B layer chunks; no form in the shape, so a statement with the reductions on is under-priced by it

H100.note: the prompt and the output proved as one statement, per proved position, the five reductions on; read from the constants file and from nothing else, so a row priced on it is recordable
